findings.text: A kernel parameter operations record exposes get and set handling for the workqueue watchdog threshold, allowing runtime reconfiguration through the parameter layer.

Setting the watchdog threshold first clears the stored value and cancels the timer synchronously; a zero request leaves the facility disabled while a nonzero request stores the new limit, refreshes the touched stamp, and arms the timer that many seconds in the future.

The threshold parameter setter accepts an unsigned integer, rejects values that would overflow the jiffy range, applies live reconfiguration when the default per CPU queue already exists, and otherwise only stores the value for later initialization.
Watchdog initialization has an active variant that registers a deferrable timer and then applies the stored threshold, and an inert variant that performs no action, selected at build time.
Bottom half pool kickers are irq work callbacks where the normal tier raises the tasklet softirq and the high priority tier raises the high softirq.
Unbound mask restriction keeps the current mask unchanged with a warning when intersection with the candidate would be empty, and otherwise narrows the mask to the intersection.

Per CPU pool setup records the CPU number, mirrors per CPU membership into two attribute masks, stores niceness, enables strict affinity, derives the NUMA node from the CPU, and assigns a pool identifier while holding the global pool mutex.

Early workqueue initialization runs at boot to allocate core masks, establish the system affinity pod, create CPU and bottom half pools, prepare standard attributes, and instantiate the set of system queues, aborting if any essential allocation fails.

Early initialization copies online and possible membership into dedicated masks, restricts the unbound mask by housekeeping domain and command line list, preserves a requested copy, derives an isolated set, enables power efficient default under full tickless housekeeping, and builds a single system pod spanning all possible CPUs on no node.
Standard pools use two niceness tiers with matching irq kickers, and default unbound plus ordered attributes are prepared per tier with ordering enabled only for the ordered set.

The intensive work threshold initializer starts a dedicated release worker, preserves a user supplied value, and otherwise derives a default from processor speed estimated from loop calibration with a ten millisecond base scaled up toward one second on slow machines.

Late initialization proceeds from threshold setup through locked node repair and early rescuer creation, then bottom half pseudo worker creation for every possible CPU, online CPU worker creation clearing disassociation, unbound pool worker creation, marking the subsystem online, and finally watchdog start.
The global pool mutex serializes pool identifier assignment, late node hint repair with rescuer creation, and topology refresh; a per workqueue mutex nests inside during node concurrency updates.

Worker fields carry stability rules where idle or busy linkage plus scheduled list plus flags are under pool lock, current execution state plus last active stamp under a kernel state lock, sleeping flag under scheduler lock, task plus identifier plus rescue target immutable after creation, and pool anchor plus worker list node under allocator or pool rules.

The worker record contains a shared idle list versus busy hash linkage, current work plus function plus queue plus runtime plus start time plus color, a sleeping indicator, a last function hint, a scheduled list, task and pool anchors, a pool membership node, last activity stamp, flags, numeric identifier, a fixed size description area, and a rescuer target queue.

Pod construction groups every possible CPU by a pairwise sharing predicate, assigning each CPU either to an earlier compatible pod or to a fresh pod, then allocates per pod CPU masks and node records and populates them from the assignment.

Sharing predicates define per CPU isolation as never sharing, symmetric threading siblings via thread mask membership, cache shard sharing via common cache plus equal shard identifier, and NUMA sharing via equal node number.

Last level cache sharding counts distinct cores by thread group leaders, chooses a shard count near a target size with at least one shard, distributes remainder cores over leading large shards, fills shards in CPU order without splitting threads, inherits sibling assignment from the group leader, and validates the final cursor.

Topology initialization builds CPU, threading, cache, cache shard, and NUMA pod types with shard precomputation between cache and shard stages, marks topology ready, then under lock refreshes every queue on every online CPU and updates node concurrency for unbound queues.
Flushing system wide queues emits a deprecation warning with stack trace, indicating future prohibition.
Boot command parsing for unbound CPUs clears the mask and warns on malformed input while still reporting success to the init parser, and a zero cache shard size is corrected to one with a warning.

Early and late bring up treat missing allocations or missing system queues or missing workers as fatal, rescuer creation failure only warns, and shard assignment skips an out of range sibling leader with a one time warning plus a final shard count check.

System queue set includes per CPU, high priority, long, unbound, default, freezable, power efficient, combined freezable power efficient, bottom half, high priority bottom half, and default long variants.
Late initialization, early initialization, and topology initialization are exported boot entry points invoked in subsystem order.
The internal header defines a once only inclusion guard.
